questions.q: What is the maximum number of callouts a single Apex transaction can make to an HTTP request or API call?
questions.explain: The Apex Developer Guide's execution governors and limits reference caps a single transaction at 100 HTTP/API callouts.

questions.q: What is the maximum cumulative timeout for all callouts made within a single Apex transaction?
options: 120 seconds, additive across every callout in the transaction
There is no cumulative limit, only a per-callout limit
questions.explain: The 120-second cumulative timeout adds up across every callout made in the transaction, independent of each individual callout's own timeout setting.

questions.q: What is the default per-callout timeout, and what is the maximum you can configure with setTimeout()?
options: There is no default; a timeout must always be set explicitly
questions.explain: The default timeout is 10 seconds; it can be customized between a minimum of 1 millisecond and a maximum of 120,000 milliseconds (120 seconds).

questions.q: Why doesn't HTTP callout processing time count against the org's long-running request limit (over 5 seconds of execution time)?
options: Because callouts are always completed in under 5 seconds
Because a callout spends most of its time waiting on a remote system rather than consuming Salesforce's own compute
Because the long-running request limit was deprecated
Because callouts run in a separate org entirely
questions.explain: The long-running request limit targets synchronous Salesforce compute time; callout wait time is excluded from that calculation specifically because it isn't consuming Salesforce's own processing.

questions.q: According to the transaction-ordering rule, in what order must a callout and a DML statement in the same transaction occur?
options: DML must always happen before the callout
The callout must happen before any pending DML, async work, or email in that transaction — not after
Order doesn't matter as long as both happen within 120 seconds
DML and callouts can never occur in the same transaction under any circumstance
questions.explain: A transaction can't make a callout while it has pending uncommitted DML, async work, or email — the callout must come first, or the DML must be deferred to a separate async transaction.
